subject: Daily AcreetionOS Update -- September 05, 2026
body:
Daily AcreetionOS Update - September 05, 2026

Welcome to today's edition of the AcreetionOS newsletter. We are a community-driven, user-friendly Linux distribution based on Arch Linux, featuring the Cinnamon desktop environment and a firm commitment to privacy with no telemetry. Our small but dedicated team, led by co-developers Natalie Cole-Clift Spiva and Darren Clift from Spokane, Washington, continues to push forward with improvements to both the core distribution and our supporting infrastructure.

On the development side, significant progress was made this week on our CI/CD pipelines. The acreetionos-immutable project received several commits addressing release workflow issues, including fixes to block-scalar indentation that was breaking workflow validation and improvements to how the GitHub release creation step handles the checkout process. These changes should make our release pipeline more reliable and easier to maintain going forward.

The AcreetionOS-Xlibre build received a welcome addition with the inclusion of firefox-ublock-origin in the build process. This ensures that users of our XLibre-based images will have immediate access to effective ad-blocking capabilities right out of the box. Additionally, the main acreetionos-code repository saw a merge from the release-1 branch addressing a geocode-glib update conflict that should streamline future updates.

Our infrastructure team has been working on maintaining our self-hosted GitLab instance, which serves as a central hub for development activities. A recent re-trigger of the GitLab mirror with a deploy key fix ensures that our code synchronization between GitHub and GitLab remains stable. Shellcheck linting was also explicitly added to top-level scripts in the acreetionos-code-acreetionos repository, improving code quality standards across the project.

In broader Linux community news, Grml released version 2026.09 this week, continuing to provide their specialist Debian-based distribution for system administrators and rescue purposes. Security updates were also issued by multiple distributions, including important patches from Debian for chromium, firefox-esr, and pcre2, while Fedora addressed vulnerabilities in cockpit, expat, kernel, and several other packages. Users of other distributions should check their package managers for available updates.

For our Tips and Highlights section, we encourage all AcreetionOS users to regularly update their systems using the standard Arch Linux rolling release model. Running sudo pacman -Syu periodically ensures you receive the latest features, bug fixes, and security patches. Our distribution maintains full compatibility with the Arch User Repository (AUR), giving users access to thousands of additional packages beyond the core repositories.

If you are new to AcreetionOS, remember that our Calamares-based installer provides a smooth installation experience, developed and maintained by our very own Darren Clift who contributes to the upstream Calamares project. The minimum system requirements include a 64-bit processor, 2GB of RAM, and 20GB of storage space, making it accessible for a wide range of hardware configurations.

We invite community members to join our Discord server at discord.gg/VHqQkJASw7 for real-time support and discussions. Whether you are troubleshooting an installation issue, sharing your custom configurations, or just want to connect with fellow Linux enthusiasts, our community is here to welcome you. We also maintain presence on X (formerly Twitter) and Bluesky for those who prefer different social platforms.

Thank you for reading today's newsletter and for your continued support of the AcreetionOS project. Every user, contributor, and community member plays a vital role in making this distribution what it is. We look forward to sharing more updates tomorrow, and as always, happy computing from the entire AcreetionOS team in Spokane, Washington.
